scope: Collected Budget Council findings, financial source metadata and selected reviewed summaries. PDFs are not read live; no complete transaction ledger is included.

records.title: Finance Director agreement authorized
records.text: Council authorized the City Manager to execute the Finance Director employment agreement for Travis Hickey. White moved and Voigt seconded.
records.limitation: Checked against the supplied City minutes. Salary and benefit figures in the earlier briefing are from the agreement and staff report; the minutes do not restate those figures.

records.title: Deputy City Manager agreement authorized
records.text: Council authorized execution of Kari Mendoza’s Deputy City Manager employment agreement. Mendoza recused. Voigt moved and White seconded.
records.limitation: Checked against the supplied City minutes. Salary and benefit figures in the earlier briefing are from the agreement and staff report; the minutes do not restate those figures.

records.title: Oak Valley Parkway traffic-signal award approved
records.text: Council awarded Calpromax Engineering the Oak Valley Parkway/Palm Avenue signal work for $847,090 plus $84,710 contingency, totaling $931,800. Voigt moved and White seconded.
records.limitation: Checked against the supplied City minutes. Authorization does not establish payment, completed work, or later implementation.

records.title: Holiday-decoration and accounting contract capacity increased
records.text: Within the consent vote, Council increased Dekra-Lite’s aggregate ceiling from $260,000 to $500,000 within the approved budget, with up to 5% amendment/change-order authority. The LSL accounting agreement increased by $100,000 from $65,000 to $165,000.
records.limitation: Checked against the supplied City minutes. The Dekra-Lite motion requests no additional appropriation. Contract ceilings are not proof of expenditure.

records.title: Highland Springs smart-signal construction awarded
records.text: Council awarded California Professional Engineering the signal smart-technology work for $723,517 plus $72,352 contingency, totaling $795,869. Voigt moved and Lara seconded.
records.limitation: Checked against the supplied City minutes. Authorization does not establish payment, completed work, or later implementation.

records.title: Playground and field-lighting equipment purchases approved
records.text: Council approved $972,933.56 in combined equipment purchases for Sports Park and Wildflower Park, with maximum combined purchase authority of $1,021,580.23. The final motion uses remaining CIP P-04 savings for the playground purchase and contingency instead of CIP P25-05. Lara moved and Voigt seconded.
records.limitation: Checked against the supplied City minutes. Equipment purchasing authority is distinct from installation/construction costs and actual expenditure.

records.title: Temporary Trevino skate amenities authorized for competitive bidding
records.text: Council authorized competitive bidding, agreements and a purchase order up to $120,000. Funding is $72,609.98 in savings ($67,462.16 from P-09 and $5,147.82 from P-20) plus $47,390.02 from P27-01. The motion requires staff to bring back a budget adjustment reallocating the funding source. Voigt moved and White seconded.
records.limitation: Checked against the supplied City minutes. This is procurement authority, not a direct award to American Ramp or proof that a contract, installation, or funding-source adjustment has been completed.

records.title: Police station: Phase I services authorized
records.text: Council approved the Tilden-Coil agreement with a $5,437,851 overall ceiling subject to phase funding and authorization. The present authorization is $219,752 plus $21,975 contingency, totaling $241,727 for Phase I. Staff excluded the optional $18,000 modeling service from this award and said a corrected agreement would be used. Later phases require Council authorization.
records.limitation: Transcript-based finding; approved October 20 minutes not yet collected. The roughly $88.5 million project estimate is not fully funded: staff described about $8.5 million available and about $80 million unfunded. This action is not a construction award or proof of expenditure; an architect award will return separately.

records.title: IOA Championship sponsorship approved
records.text: Council approved sponsorship of the 2027 IOA Championship up to $80,000 and authorized a sponsorship agreement, with a public-purpose finding. Lara voted no; Fenn, Martinez, White, and Voigt voted yes. Discussion covered youth and senior pro-am participation, promotion, deliverables, and post-event reporting.
records.limitation: Transcript-based finding; approved October 20 minutes not yet collected. This is an authorization ceiling, not a verified payment or measured economic return. Staff time and promotional support are additional matters to track in the agreement and event report.

records.title: Downtown Phase I design directed
records.text: Council directed the City Manager to proceed with the Phase I concept as discussed and amend the STB Landscape Architects contract. Staff corrected the concept cost to $15,450; with $53,400 additional design services, the stated combined STB design cost is $68,850. Construction funding and a later award will return to Council.
records.limitation: Transcript-based finding; approved October 20 minutes not yet collected. The $2–3 million construction figure is a planning estimate, not an award or appropriation. Staff discussed existing downtown CIP resources and future funding options; no dedicated construction funding was authorized by this motion.

records.title: Tyler three-year renewal approved
records.text: Council approved and authorized execution of the three-year Tyler Technologies amendment. Staff corrected the amendment amount from $631,892.93 to $631,892.87 and separately described $346,144.50 in estimated wastewater usage-based card fees. Staff said no additional appropriation was requested.
records.limitation: Transcript-based finding; approved October 20 minutes not yet collected. Wastewater transaction fees are variable estimates outside the amendment, not a fixed vendor price. The combined planning figure is $978,037.37 after the six-cent correction, not verified expenditure.

records.title: Warrants approved separately
records.text: Council discussed missing Treasurer signatures. The City Attorney said this should not prevent payment and described possible retroactive ratification by the future Treasurer. Council then approved G.1 separately.
records.limitation: Transcript-based finding; approved October 20 minutes not yet collected. The transcript does not establish that later Treasurer ratification occurred or independently reconcile the warrant payments.

records.title: Second budget workshop: sponsorship direction
records.text: The minutes record direction to add $45,000 to Council sponsorships and return with a Donation and Sponsorship Policy. The transcript records staff direction to consolidate donations and sponsorships into one $273,300 line rather than earmark individual events.
records.limitation: This was budget preparation, not final budget adoption or approval of individual sponsorship payments.

records.title: Forecast alternatives before budget adoption
records.text: Council requested another workshop, different forecasting scenarios, a review of sponsorships and a future discussion of Council benefits. Staff's presentation modeled a proposed $75 million police-station bond with debt service beginning in FY2030.
records.limitation: The bond was a forecast assumption, not an issuance authorization. Obtain the presentation and assumptions before reproducing scenario totals.

records.title: Revenue outlook and phase-two direction
records.text: Council received and filed GrassrootsLab's Revenue Outlook and Review of Options report and directed staff to proceed with phase two. The minutes record a 3-0 vote.
records.limitation: The report and supporting packet are now linked. Receipt and phase-two direction did not itself enact a tax or establish the results of later outreach.

records.title: Fire-service and pavement funding decisions
records.text: The minutes record separate 4-0 approvals of the Fire Station 106 equipment/staffing cost-share agreement, rescission of the $1,383,753 fire-engine purchase order in favor of including the engine in the County engine-use agreement, and Pavement Management Program Scenario 1 aligned with the adopted FY2026–30 CIP.
records.limitation: Supporting reports and agreements are now archived. The rescinded purchase-order amount is not a verified saving; actual payments and later engine-use costs remain distinct.

records.title: Midyear budget: amendments and timing effects
records.text: Council unanimously received and filed the FY2024–25 midyear report and approved its amendments. The transcript explains that a one-time sales-tax audit correction affected receipts and that delayed County fire-service invoices affected reported expenditure timing. Council requested a list of authorized but unfilled positions.
records.limitation: Interim receipts and delayed payments do not establish recurring revenue growth or permanent savings. Amendment schedules and audited actuals are needed for reconciliation.

records.title: FY2021 financial report received
records.text: Council unanimously received and filed the FY2021 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report and associated reports.
records.limitation: Receiving an audit does not itself authorize new spending.

records.title: Midyear budget adjustments and wastewater vehicle
records.text: Council unanimously approved the CIP, wastewater and General Fund adjustments in the item attachments and ratified a $41,943.78 emergency vehicle purchase.
records.limitation: The attached schedules define the budget adjustments; this is not a total-cost estimate for every project discussed.

records.title: Pension funding and PARS strategy
records.text: Council unanimously approved Example 2 of the pension funding policy with an active moderate investment strategy for the PARS 115 Trust.
records.limitation: An investment-policy decision does not establish subsequent returns.

records.title: Development-impact-fee study preparation
records.text: Council directed preparation of nexus-study RFPs, inclusion of DIF updates in the FY2022-23 budget and a follow-up agenda discussion.
records.limitation: The direction did not adopt revised impact-fee rates.

records.title: CFD administration contract amendment
records.text: Council unanimously approved the second amendment with Webb Municipal Finance for CFD administration and reporting services.
records.limitation: Read the amendment for its scope and costs; this action did not establish a new CFD.

records.title: Cherry Festival sponsorship approved
records.text: Council unanimously approved $100,000 for the 2022 Cherry Festival and directed staff to establish a multiyear sponsorship contract.
records.limitation: The approved 2022 allocation is distinct from a future multiyear contract.

records.title: Compensation plan tabled
records.text: Council unanimously tabled the compensation plan and salary table and requested additional information about positions being considered for increases.
records.limitation: The proposed salary changes were not approved at this meeting.

records.title: Grant policies approved
records.text: Council unanimously approved the City grant policies and procedures.
records.limitation: Policy approval does not establish that a particular grant was awarded or spent.

records.title: Grant-writing assistance authorized
records.text: Council unanimously approved a one-time $15,000 request for grant-writing assistance with Townsend Public Affairs and authorized execution of the agreement.
records.limitation: This is a service authorization, not a grant award or evidence of payment.

records.title: PARS 115 Trust investment policy approved
records.text: Council unanimously approved the PARS 115 Trust Investment Policy, following the January pension-policy decision.
records.limitation: Approval of an investment policy does not establish investment performance or subsequent contributions.

records.title: Stewart Park design authorization: $647,971 ceiling
records.text: Council approved 4-0 the PlaceWorks design-services agreement for Stewart Park, with a not-to-exceed amount of $647,971.
records.limitation: The authorization ceiling is distinct from actual payments, construction costs and later contract amendments.

records.title: Transit free-fare program resolution approved
records.text: Council approved 4-0 the LCTOP resolution for a $102,000 Free Fare Program Promotion and authorized the associated certifications, assurances and agent form.
records.limitation: Program authorization is not proof of reimbursement, final spending or ridership results.

records.title: Street rehabilitation projects authorized for bidding
records.text: Council approved street selection for FY21/22 CIP R-08 and R-09 and authorized staff to finalize the bid package and solicit bids, 4-0.
records.limitation: Bid authorization is not a construction contract award or a final project cost.

records.title: Nvoicepay presentation received and filed
records.text: Council unanimously received and filed the Nvoicepay presentation. The published agenda identifies this as item 11; the minutes reorder it with Noble Creek Vistas.
records.limitation: Receiving a presentation does not by itself establish a new procurement authorization, realized savings or payment performance.

records.title: FY2025–26 budget and five-year CIP adopted
records.text: Council unanimously adopted the appropriation limit, FY2025–26 operating budget and five-year Capital Improvement Plan, and approved the requisition list.
records.limitation: Budget adoption authorizes spending; it does not establish actual expenditure or completion of every listed project.

records.title: CFD refunding authorization with White recused
records.text: Council approved the CFD 93-1 refunding actions 4-0, with White recused. The associated Public Improvement Authority authorization set a $30 million principal ceiling.
records.limitation: A ceiling is not an issued principal amount or realized saving. The minutes print a modified savings threshold of $21; consult the actual bond documents before interpreting that notation.

records.title: Wastewater revenue refunding authorized
records.text: Council unanimously approved documents for Wastewater Revenue Refunding Bonds, Series 2025A, with an $80 million principal ceiling, alongside the Public Improvement Authority action.
records.limitation: Authorization does not establish final pricing, issuance proceeds, debt-service savings or closing costs.

records.title: As-needed bond counsel agreement approved
records.text: Council unanimously approved Stradling Yocca Carlson & Rauth for as-needed bond counsel services from July 15, 2025 through June 30, 2030, with compensation based on services rendered under the agreement.
records.limitation: This is a professional-services authorization, not approval to issue a particular bond or proof of total fees paid.

records.title: Urban Futures advisory agreement approved
records.text: Council unanimously approved Urban Futures for as-needed financial advisory services from July 15, 2025 through July 15, 2030, with compensation based on services rendered.
records.limitation: The agreement does not itself establish a bond issuance, realized savings or total payments.

records.title: FY2024 Single Audit received through consent
records.text: The consent approval included receipt and filing of the FY2024 Single Audit on federal awards. The minutes state approval but do not give a consent tally.
records.limitation: Receiving an audit is not a separate approval of every underlying expenditure or a guarantee of future compliance.

records.title: Updated debt-management policy adopted
records.text: Council unanimously approved the updated Debt Management Policy as part of the consent calendar.
records.limitation: A debt policy does not itself authorize a particular borrowing or establish subsequent compliance.

records.title: Purchasing-policy update approved
records.text: The minutes record a Voigt motion, seconded by Fenn, taking G.8 and G.15 together and approving the Purchasing Policy Update. No vote tally is stated.
records.limitation: The policy action does not establish approval or payment of a separate contract outside the authority described in the policy.

records.text: Council’s unanimous consent approval included the FY2024–25 fourth-quarter financial report and the budget adjustments in Attachment B.
records.limitation: The June 30 interim report is distinct from final audited actuals; adjustments are spending authority, not proof of payment.

records.title: Beaumont Nights: spending coverage
records.text: The collected September 1, 2026 meeting record receives the 2026 recap and directs a proposed 15-date 2027 program. Future dates and contracts remain subject to annual budgeting and contracting. This answer corpus has no reconciled three-year actual-expenditure ledger for Beaumont Nights. Do not infer spending from visits, budgets, contracts or event counts.
records.limitation: A three-year total requires year-specific expense detail, payroll/overtime scope, invoices and reconciliation. Specify calendar or fiscal years and gross cost or net cost after revenues.

records.title: FY 2026–27 adopted budget
records.text: Council adopted the FY 2026–27 budget on June 16, 2026. Projected all-fund revenues were $168 million and planned expenditures $162.5 million. General Fund planned revenues and expenditures were each $75.6 million. The General Fund is included within all funds; do not add them. These are budget plans, not actual expenditure.

records.title: Budget, authorization and actual spending
records.text: An adopted budget is spending authority. A contract ceiling is not payment. A grant application is not an award. Audited actuals differ from interim budget-to-actual reports. Compare like funds, periods and accounting bases; disclose gross versus net cost. Do not add an amendment to the amended total, or a phase authorization to its overall ceiling.
